about.title: King City Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, but the aftermath rarely feels that way. Someone in King City might slip on a wet floor near San Antonio Drive, trip on a broken step off S 1st Street, or get hurt on poorly maintained walkways along Broadway Street or Ellis Street. Whatever the setting, California law asks a hard question: did the property owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard, and did they fail to fix it or warn you? That's the heart of a premises liability claim. Because King City is a smaller community, evidence like surveillance footage or incident reports can disappear quickly if no one asks for it early. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result. We simply connect injured residents with an independent attorney who can look into the details of your fall, evaluate notice and timing, and explain your options in plain terms, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why the Details of Notice and Timing Matter

items.title: California Requires Proof of Notice
items.desc: You generally have to show the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazardous condition and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather the records and testimony needed to establish that timeline.

items.title: Evidence Fades Fast in a Small Market
items.desc: Surveillance footage at King City businesses is often overwritten within days or weeks. Acting early to request and preserve that video can make a real difference in supporting your account of the fall.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for not noticing a hazard, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present your side fairly rather than let an insurer overstate your share of blame.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in King City?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, like a public building or city sidewalk, that deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim process. Because King City has both private businesses and public facilities, it's worth getting a quick read on who owned the property where you fell.

items.question: What if the store or landlord says they didn't know about the hazard?
items.answer: That's a common response, but California law looks at what the owner reasonably should have known, not just what they admit to knowing. Things like how long a spill sat, inspection logs, or prior complaints about the same area can all speak to that. An independent attorney can help figure out what records exist and how to request them.

items.question: Does it matter that King City is a small town for gathering evidence?
items.answer: It can work both ways. Smaller businesses along corridors like Broadway Street or Ellis Street may not have formal video retention policies, so footage can be deleted sooner than in a larger city. On the other hand, local employees and witnesses are sometimes easier to reach and speak with early on, which can help build a clearer picture of what happened.
